newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Dominican survives for 22 days adrift at sea.
newsitem.headline: Dominican survives for 22 days adrift at sea.

text.p: A Dominican fisherman drifted for 22 days at sea surviving on raw fish, rainwater and his own urine until he was rescued by Hondurans on the other side of the Caribbean, authorities said on Friday.
Fisherman Thomas Garcia said he went out on a one-day fishing trip from the port of San Pedro de Marcoris in the Dominican Republic on Dec. 15, but ran out of fuel.
On Jan. 5 he was found by fishermen off the Bay Islands on Honduras' Caribbean coast, having apparently drifted some 700 miles (1100 km) across the ocean, past Haiti and Jamaica.

"The fisherman assures us that he was adrift at sea for 22 days after he ran out of fuel and could not return to the shores of his country," Allan Eris, a local official from Honduras' Bay Islands, told Reuters.
Garcia spent Christmas and New Year's Day aboard his 18-foot (5.5 metre)-long fiberglass boat, and said he was close to death when he was rescued.

"I had to eat raw fish and drink the milk of a coconut I found floating, and on Dec. 24 and 25 it rained," the man told the Honduran newspaper El Tiempo. "After that I had to drink my own urine to survive."
"Just when I thought I was going to die some Honduran fishermen found me," Garcia said. "I don't know how I survived."
He was taken straight to a hospital and was due to be returned to the Dominican Republic as soon as he was fully recovered, officials said.
